name: Business, Economics and Finance
description: A decision-grade blueprint for markets, organizations, strategy, operations, economics, and financial evidence.

guidance: Start from the decision, stakeholder, time horizon, unit of analysis, and comparison baseline.
Separate reported performance, calculated results, management interpretation, external context, and recommendation.
Reconcile metric definitions, currency, nominal versus real values, period coverage, population, and denominator before comparison.
Organize analysis around performance, drivers, operating model, market context, risks, scenarios, and decision implications only where supported.
Do not infer causality from movement, ranking, or correlation; label hypotheses and competing explanations.
Use charts for comparable trends, segments, distributions, bridges, or relationships with explicit units and coverage.
Recommendations must name rationale, dependency, risk, time horizon, and a measurable validation signal.

sections.title: Decision Context and Executive Answer
sections.purpose: Orient the decision-maker, define the evidence perimeter, and answer the objective with the most material business implications.

blocks.title: Decision and Evidence Profile
instructions: State entity, market, period, currency or units, population, source coverage, and material comparability gaps.

blocks.title: Executive Answer
instructions: Answer the objective with the strongest performance signal, primary driver or constraint, decision implication, and uncertainty.
Distinguish verified results from source assertions and interpretation.

blocks.title: Decision-Critical Findings
instructions: Present non-overlapping findings about magnitude, direction, segment, economics, operations, risk, or opportunity with baselines and units where available.

sections.title: Performance, Drivers and Operating Context
sections.purpose: Explain what changed or differs, the scale of the result, and which evidenced factors are associated with it.

blocks.title: Performance and Driver Analysis
instructions: Compare against the correct prior period, plan, peer, or segment baseline and preserve currency, unit, denominator, and scope.
Treat proposed drivers as hypotheses unless the evidence supports attribution.

blocks.title: Value Driver Chain
instructions: Map one supported chain from input or market condition through operating mechanism to outcome; label unverified links.

sections.title: Market Context, Scenarios and Trade-offs
sections.purpose: Place internal evidence in its relevant external context and test which assumptions could change the conclusion.

blocks.title: Context and Scenario Analysis
instructions: Explain relevant market, policy, competitor, customer, or macro conditions and distinguish observed conditions from modeled scenarios.
Identify assumptions, sensitivities, trade-offs, and break points without inventing forecasts.

blocks.title: Comparable Performance Evidence

chart_slot.intent: Support one decision-critical claim with comparable trend, segment, distribution, or relationship evidence.

fallback.message: No comparable quantitative business evidence is available.

instructions: Chart only values sharing compatible definitions, units, periods, and populations; expose bounded coverage and exclude decorative KPIs.

sections.title: Decision Evidence and Actions
sections.purpose: Make the evidentiary basis auditable and translate supported findings into conditional action.

blocks.title: Evidence Trail
instructions: Tie claims to exact values, periods, segments, source statements, assumptions, and source locations.

blocks.title: Decision Options
instructions: For each option state rationale, prerequisite, risk, horizon, owner or stakeholder when known, and a measurable validation signal.
Do not convert descriptive evidence into prescriptive certainty.

sections.title: Risks, Limitations and Missing Evidence
sections.purpose: Identify the uncertainties, comparability issues, and omitted evidence that could alter the decision.

blocks.title: Material Risks and Evidence Gaps
instructions: State only material gaps in definitions, periods, denominators, currency, inflation treatment, population, forecast assumptions, external validation, or causal evidence.
Separate decision risk from data-quality limitation.
